overview: Single-ward feasibility study, January to September 2027: named nurses screen eligible admissions with a short alcohol questionnaire once the patient is well enough, offer screen-positive patients a two-session brief motivational intervention before discharge, and attempt telephone follow-up three months after discharge. Progression criteria are stated before recruitment. The planning value for delivery came from a record whose identity check failed after the design was accepted; it is kept only as a flagged value until re-appraised.
population: Adults admitted to the 24-bed acute unit, screened once the named nurse judges them well enough and able to consent; people lacking capacity are approached only when capacity returns; stays shorter than 48 hours are excluded.
exposure: Two sessions of 20 to 30 minutes by a trained named nurse, using a pocket card of core steps, with a written plan for after discharge and an offer of referral to the community alcohol team.
procedures: Screening within the first well-enough day; consent by the named nurse; sessions in a quiet room where possible; a fidelity checklist completed after each session, with 20 percent of sessions audio-recorded and rated by a second trained nurse; two contact numbers and consent for a text reminder collected before discharge; three-month call by a nurse from another ward, up to five attempts.

outcomes.name: Uptake of the intervention
outcomes.measure: Proportion of screen-positive patients who consent and receive at least the first session before discharge
outcomes.why: The central feasibility question and the basis of any future sample size.

outcomes.name: Screening completion
outcomes.measure: Proportion of eligible admissions screened before discharge, by detention status and length of stay
outcomes.why: Shows whether the patients most at risk are reached.

outcomes.name: Delivery and fidelity
outcomes.measure: Proportion receiving both sessions; percentage of core components delivered on the checklist
outcomes.why: Separates a failed idea from failed delivery.

outcomes.name: Three-month follow-up completion
outcomes.measure: Proportion of participants reached by phone with a completed drinking question
outcomes.why: Retention is the step most likely to block a larger study.

outcomes.name: Distress after sessions
outcomes.measure: Patient-rated distress (0 to 10) before and after each session; any incident linked to a session
outcomes.why: The intervention must not add distress on an acute ward.

feasibility: About 250 eligible admissions over nine months; eleven trained nurses; sessions within approved shift time (WM-4A-2026-11); follow-up calls by nurses from another ward within normal duties.
biasMitigation: Progression criteria registered before the first patient is screened
Second-rater fidelity scoring on a random 20 percent of recorded sessions
Follow-up calls by nurses who did not deliver the sessions
Reporting by detention status and length of stay

biasFlags.label: Selective screening of cooperative patients
biasFlags.note: Nurses may screen easier patients first; screening completion by subgroup exposes this.

biasFlags.label: Planning value resting on a mismatched record
biasFlags.note: The delivery planning value came from a record whose DOI resolved to a different work; re-appraise before relying on it.

biasFlags.label: Loss to follow-up
biasFlags.note: Phone follow-up reached about half of patients elsewhere.

flags: Two process measures and one balancing measure; no effectiveness outcome is claimed
parsimony.simplestPath: One ward, one uptake proportion with its interval, traffic-light thresholds for the rest.

theoreticalFramework: None beyond the intervention's own motivational interviewing principles; TIDieR is used to describe the intervention.
summary: Feasibility protocol with uptake as the primary proportion, process, follow-up and balancing measures, and a flagged planning value.
